name: Iznik pottery
summary: Ottoman court pottery with a white quartz body, a white slip and a clear glaze. Painters used cobalt, turquoise, green and a thick tomato red for tulips, carnations and saz leaves.

philosophy.core_thesis: A bright garden of flowers can be painted flat and sharp on a white body, and it stays fresh under a clear glass-like glaze.
design_principles: Make the body of ground quartz, glass frit and a little clay, and cover it with a fine white slip.
Paint under a clear alkaline glaze, so that the colours stay bright after the firing.
Use a limited range of colours: cobalt blue, turquoise, then green, and after 1550 a raised tomato red.
Outline the motifs in a dark line and fill them in flat, with no shading.
Draw tulips, carnations, hyacinths, roses and saz leaves, and arrange them in a flowing, balanced garden.
Set an even border of waves and rocks, or a scroll, round the rim of a dish.
Fire at 900 to 1050 °C in an oxidising kiln.
anti_patterns: A buff clay body without a white slip
Soft blended shading in the petals
Overglaze enamel or gilding on top of the glaze
A thick glossy glaze that blurs the line

form.shape: Large dishes, bowls on a foot, jugs, mosque lamps, flasks and tall flat-sided bottles.
form.profile: A dish has a shallow well and a broad, flat rim; a jug has a round body and a short, strong neck.
form.foot_and_rim: A low foot ring with a pierced hole, a flat or slightly flared rim, and a lip of dark blue or turquoise.
form.proportion: Dish diameter 25 to 40 cm and a wall 4 to 7 mm thick; a jug height 20 to 30 cm.
rules: Divide a dish into a central design and a border of repeated waves.
Keep the body thin and hard, with a very white surface.
Pierce the foot ring for a cord to hang the dish.
Align the motifs with the symmetry of the form.

bodies.rule: Use a stonepaste of ground quartz, glass frit and white clay. It is hard and white, but it is not a porcelain.

methods: press moulding of tiles and flasks
painting with a brush on the slip
forming.joins: Handles and spouts are luted with slip; mosque lamps are thrown in two parts and joined.
forming.details: A white slip that shows a dark line at the edge, a hole in the foot ring, and a red that stands up slightly from the surface.

glaze.pattern: Tulips, carnations, hyacinths and saz leaves in flowing scrolls, with a border of rocks and waves.
glaze.gloss: Glassy, about 80 to 95 GU, with a clear, thin alkaline glaze.
glaze.wear: The tomato red may flake or raise a little; the glaze may craze and show a faint green tint at the thicker places.

palette.strategy: A white ground with cobalt blue, turquoise and a thick tomato red in the second half; green and black outlines add depth.

firing.kiln: A wood-fired kiln with saggars; the potters made the glaze and the body with fine quartz.
firing.scale: Dozens of potteries in Iznik worked for the Ottoman court and for export, in the 16th century.
firing.signs: A bright thin glaze, raised red, a cord hole in the foot, and sharp black outlines on a pure white ground.

pieces.form: Large dish with a central rosette and a border of waves and rocks
Jug with a round body and a loop handle, painted with saz leaves in blue
Footed bowl with tulips and carnations in red, blue and green
Flat-sided flask with spring flowers and a long neck

positive: tomato red, cobalt and turquoise on white
flat painted colours with black outline

canonical_works.work: Dish with saz leaves and flowers

evidence.title: Iznik dish in the golden horn style, about 1530

emotion.target_response: A fresh, joyful brightness: the viewer sees a flower garden in strong colours and feels the pleasure of a court garden.

use_cases: a bright floral dish or plate
a museum label on Ottoman ceramics
a prompt for a flower motif in blue, turquoise and red
avoid_when: the brief needs a plain or quiet surface
the brief needs shaded realistic flowers

modifiers.how: Remove the red, green and turquoise, change the body to porcelain and paint cobalt only.
Keep the colours and the flower motifs, change the form to flat tiles, and fit the pattern to a repeat grid.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art: Iznik pottery
